pl-l3d19c3-d1e114.summary: Asks from which penalty he redeemed us and answers: temporal and eternal. From eternal penalty by remitting the debt; from temporal penalty he will fully free us in the future, when death the last enemy is destroyed (1 Cor 15:26). We still await the redemption of the body; in soul we are already redeemed in part, not wholly: from guilt, not penalty, and not entirely from guilt, not so that it is not, but so that it does not reign.
claims: Christ redeemed us from eternal penalty by remitting the debt.
Christ will free us fully from temporal penalty in the future.
Guilt remains in us but does not reign.

pl-l3d19c3.summary: Explains from which penalty Christ redeemed us: eternal and temporal. From eternal penalty by remitting the debt; from temporal penalty he will free us fully in the future, when death the last enemy is destroyed. We still await the redemption of the body; in soul we are redeemed in part, from guilt but not penalty, and not entirely from guilt: not so that it does not exist, but so that it does not reign.
claims: Christ redeemed us from eternal penalty by remitting the debt.
Christ will free us from temporal penalty in the future.
In this life we are redeemed from guilt so that it does not reign, not so that it does not exist.
